title: Chapter 282: Jiujiang's Children's Home
html:
“Yes. Fan Yu has adopted a spider as his sister. The situation is rather complicated. If you have time, could you come to Jiujiang Children’s Home?”

“Of course. Would it be all right if I arrive between six and seven this evening?”

“No problem. Thank you for your cooperation.”

After ending the call, Chen Ge found himself dwelling on the staff member’s final question. “But what if that sister isn’t human? What if she’s a spider?”

Fan Yu had been the Haunted House’s first special visitor, and his childhood had been miserable. He had watched his father kill his mother, then seen his aunt push his father into a well. Afterward, he had spent years living under the same roof as his father’s killer.

The boy has no family left in this world. Whatever is happening, I should go and see him.

Chen Ge had planned to step into the sunlight and spin the wheel, but the call from the Children’s Home extinguished the impulse. His lunch break soon ended. He worked until 5:30 p.m., yet the stream of visitors showed no sign of thinning, forcing the team to delay closing until nearly seven.

Dusk had already fallen, and Chen Ge did not even have time to balance the day’s accounts. Once Xu Wan left, he hurried to the Children’s Home. It was his first visit. The place bore no resemblance to the cold, filthy, joyless orphanages portrayed on television. Its décor was warm and welcoming, and flowers of every kind filled the private courtyard.

“Hey, what are you doing here? We do not allow outsiders!” The gentleman who guarded the door blocked Chen Ge.

“Hello. I’m Chen Ge, a member of Fan Yu’s family. One of your staff called me this afternoon.”

“Fan Yu’s family?” The elderly gatekeeper studied Chen Ge, and his manner changed at once. “Please wait here. I’ll ask someone to come down. It’ll only take a minute.”

Rather than use a phone, the man hurried into the courtyard and shouted up the stairs. Before long, a woman about Chen Ge’s age emerged from the building. Her nurse’s uniform and gentle manner gave her a reassuring air.

“Mr. Chen, you’re finally here.” The nurse motioned for him to follow. “First, let me introduce myself. I’m Fan Yu’s ‘mother.’ You can call me Xiao Liu.”

“You’re his mother?”

“Yes. We care for many abandoned children and infants. To help them experience the warmth of a family, we let them call us Mother and Father. It isn’t compulsory, of course, but most of the children like it.” The nurse was friendly but shy, and she barely met Chen Ge’s eyes as she spoke.

“That’s wonderful. I admire that.”

Jiujiang Children’s Home felt like one large family, nothing like the orphanage Chen Ge had imagined. The nurse gave him a bright smile and was about to speak when a window across the courtyard flew open. A middle-aged man holding a tray of teacups leaned out and shouted, “Xiao Liu, wandering off again? Get back to your post and watch Jiang Ling and Fan Yu! Their conditions are getting worse!”

The man’s voice sounded angry, but Xiao Liu was not afraid. Instead, she was embarrassed. “Yes, I understand.”

The nurse led Chen Ge inside. Cheerful decorations covered the walls, and the corridor was spotless.

“Who was that? The president?” Chen Ge asked.

“That was Doctor Chen. He can be gruff, but he’s a good man. He used to work at a large clinic before coming here.”

“Doctor Chen? There’s a specialist attached to the children’s home?”

“Yes. We have doctors, nurses, nutritionists, and teachers. We each perform different duties, but all of us act as parents to the children.” Chen Ge nodded. Compared with the privately run orphanage founded by Mu Yang High School’s headmaster, this institution was far more formal. As they walked along the corridor, a door suddenly opened and two boys burst out, each tugging on the same toy.

“Jiang Jin, Jiang He! No running or shouting in the corridor—it’s past eight! Back to your room!” the nurse scolded. The boys reluctantly obeyed. Before their door closed, Chen Ge glimpsed two bedrooms and a living room shared by six children.

“This is a good place. The children have new toys and clothes.” Chen Ge examined the painted name cards on the doors. “Something puzzles me. Why do all their names begin with Jiang?”

“They’re the children of Jiujiang, so we took their surname from the city’s name,” the nurse explained with a self-conscious smile. “Of course, some arrive with names already, and we never force them to change.”

The nurse led Chen Ge to the first room on the left on the third floor. She walked in without knocking.

“President, Chen Ge is here.”

An elderly man in his sixties stood by the window, watering the plants on its sill. With his spectacles and mild appearance, he resembled a retired teacher.

“You’re finally here. Please, sit.” The man regarded Chen Ge like a long-awaited savior, which only deepened his confusion.

“Sir, what exactly happened? Has Fan Yu caused trouble here?” Chen Ge felt like a parent summoned for a private conference after school.

“I’ll be frank.” The director glanced at the nurse and asked her to close the door, as though afraid of being overheard. “You’re listed as Fan Yu’s guardian, so you must understand his condition better than we do. He isn’t sociable… How should I put it? Concepts such as family, belonging, and happiness mean nothing to him. We’ve done everything we can to help, with little success.”

Chen Ge knew Fan Yu better than most, so he understood the trouble the Children’s Home was facing. “I’m so sorry for creating all this trouble.”

The director shook his head. “That alone wouldn’t be a problem. We’ve cared for children even more withdrawn than Fan Yu. Our concern is that while we’ve been unable to improve his condition, he has begun influencing other children who are still recovering.”

“What do you mean?” Chen Ge understood why that Doctor Chen was so angry when he saw Xiao Liu.

“Sadly, many children who suffer trauma or abandonment develop psychological problems that require counseling.” The director smiled sadly. “Fan Yu is a clear example, but he continually argues with the doctor. Not only does he reject treatment, he tells the other children disturbing things. Several deteriorated after spending time with him, and we had no choice but to separate them.”
